transcript.speaker: Carla Diaz
transcript.text: Okay, thanks both for blocking this, board meeting is Thursday so I want us fully aligned on the numbers and the story before we walk in. Nate, let's start with you, where did we land on Q3?

transcript.speaker: Nate Kim
transcript.text: Sure. ARR closed Q3 at three point two million, up from two point nine at the end of Q2, so about ten percent quarter over quarter growth.

transcript.speaker: Carla Diaz
transcript.text: How does that compare to what we told the board last quarter we were targeting?

transcript.speaker: Nate Kim
transcript.text: We'd guided to three point three, so we're a bit light, about three percent under plan, mostly driven by slower new logo growth than we projected, not a retention problem.

transcript.speaker: Maya Chen
transcript.text: Right, retention's actually been the bright spot, our net revenue retention for Q3 came in at one hundred and eight percent, that's up from one oh three in Q2.

transcript.speaker: Carla Diaz
transcript.text: That's a good story to lead with honestly, expansion within the existing base is strong even if new logos are softer.

transcript.speaker: Nate Kim
transcript.text: Agreed, and gross revenue retention was ninety six percent for the quarter, so churn stayed pretty controlled, we lost a couple of small accounts but nothing structural.

transcript.speaker: Carla Diaz
transcript.text: Any accounts the board would specifically ask about? They tend to remember logos from past updates.

transcript.speaker: Maya Chen
transcript.text: Acme is one I'd flag proactively rather than let them find it in the numbers. Their usage dipped after their data engineering lead went on leave, and their renewal is coming up in a few weeks. Sam's actively managing it and we're getting them early access to the Snowflake integration to help secure the renewal.

transcript.speaker: Carla Diaz
transcript.text: Good, I'd rather we bring that up ourselves with a plan attached than have someone ask and we look flat footed. What's the ARR exposure there if it doesn't renew?

transcript.speaker: Nate Kim
transcript.text: Forty two thousand annual, so meaningful but not company threatening, less than one and a half percent of total ARR.

transcript.speaker: Carla Diaz
transcript.text: Good context to have ready if asked. What's the positive counterweight we can point to?

transcript.speaker: Maya Chen
transcript.text: Globex, definitely. Two hundred and ten seats, biggest new logo of the year, healthcare analytics space which is a new vertical proof point for us, and onboarding's going smoothly so far.

transcript.speaker: Carla Diaz
transcript.text: That's a great one to highlight, especially the new vertical angle, investors like seeing we're not a one-industry product.

transcript.speaker: Nate Kim
transcript.text: Agreed, I'll make sure Globex gets its own slide rather than getting buried in a logo grid.

transcript.speaker: Carla Diaz
transcript.text: Nate, let's talk burn and runway, that's always a top question.

transcript.speaker: Nate Kim
transcript.text: Burn was four hundred and ten thousand for the quarter, roughly flat versus Q2's four hundred and five, mostly driven by the two engineering hires we made in August. At current burn we've got nineteen months of runway.

transcript.speaker: Carla Diaz
transcript.text: Nineteen months, and that's assuming no further hiring or revenue changes?

transcript.speaker: Nate Kim
transcript.text: Right, that's the flat scenario. If we hit our Q4 hiring plan, which includes the frontend engineer we're finalizing and possibly one more backend hire in Q1, runway comes down to around seventeen months.

transcript.speaker: Carla Diaz
transcript.text: That's still comfortable, but I want us ready if someone asks about the next fundraise timeline given that number.

transcript.speaker: Nate Kim
transcript.text: I'd say we want to be back in market by roughly month twelve to fourteen of that runway to leave buffer, so sometime around next summer is when we'd start those conversations in earnest.

transcript.speaker: Carla Diaz
transcript.text: Good, let's have that answer ready but not put it in the deck proactively, no need to raise the fundraise topic before someone asks.

transcript.speaker: Maya Chen
transcript.text: Agreed, better to be prepared than to lead with it.

transcript.speaker: Carla Diaz
transcript.text: Let's talk CAC and LTV since that usually comes up too.

transcript.speaker: Nate Kim
transcript.text: CAC was around eight thousand two hundred per customer this quarter, up slightly from seventy eight hundred, mostly due to the marketing spend increase for the Q4 campaign that's technically launching just after this quarter closes, so some of that spend is showing up in Q3 without the resulting pipeline yet.

transcript.speaker: Carla Diaz
transcript.text: That's an important nuance, I don't want the board to think CAC is trending badly without that context.

transcript.speaker: Nate Kim
transcript.text: Agreed, I'll add a footnote on the slide explaining the campaign spend timing mismatch.

transcript.speaker: Maya Chen
transcript.text: And LTV to CAC ratio is still healthy, around five to one based on current retention curves, so even with CAC ticking up slightly we're well within a healthy range.

transcript.speaker: Carla Diaz
transcript.text: Good, that ratio is the number they'll actually care about more than CAC in isolation. Let's move to product. Maya, what are the highlights you want on the roadmap slide?

transcript.speaker: Maya Chen
transcript.text: Two big ones, the Snowflake integration, which is about seventy percent complete and on track for an October fifteenth beta, and the dashboard redesign, which just came out of design critique with a locked scope, drag and drop customizable layouts.

transcript.speaker: Carla Diaz
transcript.text: Any customer proof points we can attach to those, boards like to see product investment tied to real demand?

transcript.speaker: Maya Chen
transcript.text: Yes, Snowflake was directly requested by multiple customers including Acme, and the dashboard redesign came out of interviews with eight customers including Northstar, who's actually going to preview the design as a partner before we build it.

transcript.speaker: Carla Diaz
transcript.text: That's a great detail, shows we're not building in a vacuum. I'd put both of those on one slide as 'customer-driven roadmap' or something like that.

transcript.speaker: Nate Kim
transcript.text: I like that framing, ties product spend directly to retention and expansion story.

transcript.speaker: Carla Diaz
transcript.text: Let's talk headcount plan for Q4 specifically since that ties to the burn conversation.

transcript.speaker: Nate Kim
transcript.text: We're finalizing an offer for a senior frontend engineer, that's mostly to support the dashboard redesign work. Beyond that, no other planned hires this quarter unless something urgent comes up.

transcript.speaker: Maya Chen
transcript.text: That hire is close, we did the final interview a few days ago and I think we'll have an answer by end of week.

transcript.speaker: Carla Diaz
transcript.text: Good, let's mention headcount is measured and tied directly to roadmap priorities rather than growing for growth's sake, boards like hearing that discipline.

transcript.speaker: Nate Kim
transcript.text: Agreed, I'll frame the headcount slide that way.

transcript.speaker: Carla Diaz
transcript.text: Let's talk about anticipated tough questions. What do we think they'll push on hardest this time?

transcript.speaker: Nate Kim
transcript.text: Probably the new logo growth miss versus the three point three target, they'll want to understand if that's a pipeline problem or a close rate problem.

transcript.speaker: Maya Chen
transcript.text: It's more pipeline volume honestly, our close rate on qualified opportunities actually held steady around twenty eight percent, we just had fewer opportunities enter the pipeline this quarter than planned.

transcript.speaker: Carla Diaz
transcript.text: Do we know why pipeline volume was light?

transcript.speaker: Maya Chen
transcript.text: Partly timing, our big Q4 campaign was intentionally held for October rather than September so it wouldn't overlap with a slower late-summer buying cycle, so some of what would've been Q3 pipeline is really just shifted into Q4.

transcript.speaker: Carla Diaz
transcript.text: That's a defensible answer as long as we're confident Q4 actually delivers, otherwise it looks like an excuse in hindsight.

transcript.speaker: Nate Kim
transcript.text: Fair, I'd want us to genuinely believe that before we say it in the room.

transcript.speaker: Maya Chen
transcript.text: I do believe it, the campaign's fully built and launching October first, and early creative testing results were strong, testimonial-led ads nearly doubled click through versus our old messaging.

transcript.speaker: Carla Diaz
transcript.text: Okay, I'm comfortable with that answer then, as long as we're honest that Q4 needs to prove it out. What else might they push on?

transcript.speaker: Nate Kim
transcript.text: Possibly competitive positioning, there's been more noise from a couple of well-funded competitors in adjacent analytics categories.

transcript.speaker: Maya Chen
transcript.text: I'd point to win rate against named competitors, we're still winning the majority of competitive deals we're in, mostly on ease of setup and time to first dashboard, that hasn't slipped.

transcript.speaker: Carla Diaz
transcript.text: Good, let's have that win rate number ready even if it's not on the main slide, I don't want to be searching for it live if someone asks.

transcript.speaker: Nate Kim
transcript.text: I'll pull the exact number from the CRM and have it ready as a backup slide in the appendix.

transcript.speaker: Carla Diaz
transcript.text: Perfect. Let's talk deck structure now that we've covered the substance. What's the current slide order?

transcript.speaker: Nate Kim
transcript.text: Financial summary first, ARR, retention, burn and runway. Then the customer wins and risk slide with Globex and Acme. Then the customer-driven roadmap slide Maya described. Then headcount. Then a Q4 outlook slide.

transcript.speaker: Carla Diaz
transcript.text: That order makes sense, leads with the numbers, contextualizes the risk honestly, then shows we're investing intentionally in product and people.

transcript.speaker: Maya Chen
transcript.text: Agreed, and I think the Q4 outlook slide should reference the campaign explicitly given the pipeline question we just talked through.

transcript.speaker: Carla Diaz
transcript.text: Good call, let's make sure that's explicit rather than implied.

transcript.speaker: Nate Kim
transcript.text: I'll get a full draft of the deck to both of you by tomorrow so we have a day to review before Thursday.

transcript.speaker: Carla Diaz
transcript.text: Perfect, let's plan a quick run through Wednesday afternoon, maybe thirty minutes, just to rehearse answers to the tougher questions out loud.

transcript.speaker: Maya Chen
transcript.text: Works for me, verbalizing it once before the actual meeting always helps me sound less rehearsed and more natural in the room.

transcript.speaker: Nate Kim
transcript.text: Agreed, I'll send a calendar invite for Wednesday at three.

transcript.speaker: Carla Diaz
transcript.text: Great. Let's recap. Nate sends the full draft deck tomorrow, including the win rate appendix slide and the CAC footnote we discussed.

transcript.speaker: Nate Kim
transcript.text: Confirmed.

transcript.speaker: Carla Diaz
transcript.text: Maya, can you get me the exact customer quotes or details for the Snowflake and dashboard redesign customer-driven slide by tomorrow as well, so Nate has everything he needs to finalize that slide?

transcript.speaker: Maya Chen
transcript.text: Yep, I'll pull those together today and send them over.

transcript.speaker: Carla Diaz
transcript.text: Great, and we all meet Wednesday at three to rehearse. I think we're in good shape, this was a productive session.

transcript.speaker: Nate Kim
transcript.text: Agreed, feeling much more prepared than I did an hour ago.

transcript.speaker: Maya Chen
transcript.text: Same, thanks both, talk Wednesday.

transcript.speaker: Carla Diaz
transcript.text: Thanks everyone, talk soon.

summary.overview: Carla, Nate, and Maya prepped the Q3 board deck ahead of Thursday's board meeting, reviewing ARR growth of 10% QoQ to $3.2M (slightly under the $3.3M guided target), strong net revenue retention of 108%, and controlled churn. The team planned how to proactively address the Acme renewal risk and highlight the Globex win as proof of expansion into a new vertical. They also worked through burn rate, an 19-month runway (17 months under the Q4 hiring plan), CAC/LTV context, and rehearsed answers to anticipated tough questions about new logo growth and competitive pressure. The session closed with a plan to finalize the deck and hold a rehearsal run-through Wednesday.
bullet_points: 📈 Q3 ARR: $3.2M, up 10% QoQ, ~3% under the $3.3M guided target
💚 Net revenue retention 108% (up from 103% in Q2); gross retention 96%
⚠️ Acme renewal risk flagged proactively: $42K ARR exposure, <1.5% of total ARR
🎉 Globex highlighted as biggest new logo of the year, proof of new vertical (healthcare analytics)
💸 Burn $410K in Q3, 19 months runway flat, 17 months under Q4 hiring plan
🧮 CAC $8,200 (up slightly due to Q4 campaign spend timing), LTV:CAC still ~5:1
🗺️ Roadmap framed as customer-driven: Snowflake integration and dashboard redesign both tied to specific customer requests
🎤 Wednesday 3pm rehearsal scheduled to practice answers on pipeline miss and competitive positioning
